hero.lead: A nation of 39 million that has cut its public debt from 69% to 50.5% of GDP in four years and won back the bond market, while three in four citizens cannot always count on enough good food.

stats.label: Public debt to GDP, 2025, from 69% in 2021

capital.heading: Angola has cut its debt and won the market back. Next, food on every table.

record.text: Eurobond, March 2026: $1.5 billion of notes due 2033 and $1 billion of notes due 2037, priced 24 March 2026
Eurobond, May 2026: $600 million of notes due 2031 and $900 million of notes due 2037, priced 20 May 2026, with a tender offer for older notes
Public debt, % of GDP, 2025, down from 69% in 2021
Oil-collateralised debt owed to China, 2025, down from about $16.3 billion in 2020
DFC loan for the Lobito Atlantic Railway, signed December 2025; with $200 million from DBSA, financial close reported in July 2026

register.name: Eurobond, dual tranche
register.detail: Priced 20 May 2026 · $600 million of notes due 2031 · $900 million of notes due 2037
register.note: Launched with a tender offer for the notes due 2028 and 2029, capped at $750 million
register.text: The second Eurobond sale of 2026, launched with a tender offer for the notes due 2028 and 2029, so part of the new money retires older debt.

register.name: Eurobond, dual tranche
register.detail: Priced 24 March 2026 · $1.5 billion of notes due 2033 · $1 billion of notes due 2037
register.note: Launched with a tender offer for the notes due 2028, capped at $500 million
register.text: Launched with a tender offer for the notes due 2028, so the new money also refinances the old.

register.name: Eurobond, dual tranche
register.detail: Priced October 2025 · $1 billion of 5-year notes · $750 million of 10-year notes
register.note: Two tranches, of five and ten years
register.text: A $1.75 billion sale of notes in two tranches, of five and ten years, ahead of the two sales of 2026.

register.name: Foodtec Naval G loan
register.detail: Approved 1 October 2026 · Senior A loan · Pending signing
register.text: An IFC loan of up to €40 million to Naval Holding for the €57 million expansion of Foodtec Industria Alimentar, a food manufacturer in Angola that runs a wheat mill and pasta lines. It finances food made in Angola, the standard that sets the nation’s Coverage.

register.name: Carrinho Group loan
register.detail: Approved 17 June 2026 · Senior loan · Pending disbursement
register.note: Flour mill, warehouse, central kitchen and trucks
register.text: An IFC loan of up to $40 million toward the $52.1 million expansion of the Carrinho Group, an Angolan food producer with 19 factories at the mouth of the Lobito corridor: a larger wheat flour mill, a warehouse in Benguela, a central kitchen in Luanda and new trucks. It finances food made in Angola, the standard that sets the nation’s Coverage.

register.name: Debt-for-education swap
register.detail: Guarantees approved 5 March 2026 · IBRD policy-based guarantee · MIGA second-loss guarantee
register.note: $240 million IBRD guarantee and a MIGA second-loss guarantee
register.text: A $400 million commercial loan, covered by the two guarantees, is meant to prepay costly commercial debt. The World Bank says the savings will go toward expanding access to education.

register.name: Development Policy Loan, 2026
register.detail: Approved 5 March 2026 · Development policy loan
register.note: Budget support for reforms; part of a package of about $1.1 billion
register.text: A $750 million development policy loan, approved with the guarantee for the debt-for-education swap, for reforms that promote inclusive growth and job creation.

register.name: Huila-Cunene Interconnection Project
register.detail: Approved 21 November 2025 · P512716
register.text: World Bank financing for the Huíla-Cunene interconnection, in the south of the country. It matters for energy.

register.name: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience Project
register.detail: Approved 21 November 2025 · Multi-phase programmatic approach · P507385
register.note: Preparedness and response to health emergencies
register.text: A World Bank loan for the nation’s preparedness and response to health emergencies. It matters for health.

register.name: Angola Youth Employment Opportunities Project
register.detail: Approved March 2025
register.text: World Bank financing for entrepreneurship and labour-market programmes, from which approximately 500,000 people are expected to benefit. It matters for livelihood.

register.name: Enhancing the Social Protection System for Human Capital and Resilience
register.detail: Investment project financing · Loan agreement signed December 2024 · Closing date 31 October 2029
register.text: Expands human capital and household resilience while strengthening the social protection system.

register.name: Secondary Cities Support Program
register.detail: Program-for-Results · Loan agreement signed 13 December 2024 · Closing date 31 December 2029
register.text: Strengthens the national housing programme so that secondary cities can fund and improve infrastructure, housing and services.

register.name: Second Green, Resilient, Inclusive Growth and Diversification Development Policy Loan
register.detail: Loan agreement signed 25 October 2024 · Closing date 31 December 2026
register.text: Supports green, resilient and inclusive growth through economic reform, fiscal and financial stability, social protection and climate-resilient markets.

register.name: Digital Acceleration Project
register.detail: World Bank factsheet, 27 June 2024 · $300 million IBRD loan
register.text: Broadens digital inclusion and the adoption of digital tools to grow the digital economy.

register.name: Human Resources Capacity for Universal Health Coverage
register.detail: Approved 22 June 2023 · Investment project financing · Closing date 31 December 2028
register.text: Increases the capacity and availability of the health workforce.

register.name: Accelerating Economic Diversification and Job Creation
register.detail: Announced 2 June 2023 · Approved by the World Bank Group Board that week
register.text: Attracts private investment and climate-resilient growth for small firms in sectors other than oil.

register.name: Smallholder Agricultural Transformation Project
register.detail: Approved June 2022 · IBRD (MOSAP 3)
register.text: Raises farm productivity and climate resilience for smallholder farmers. It is aimed at the standard that holds the nation lowest: food.

register.name: Climate Resilience and Water Security (RECLIMA)
register.detail: Approved 30 March 2022
register.note: Co-financed by AFD with a euro loan equivalent to $150 million
register.text: Improves water supply and water resource management for climate resilience in Zaire, Benguela, Huíla, Cuanza Sul, Cuando Cubango, Cunene, Namibe and Luanda, for nearly 1.2 million people.

register.name: Girls Empowerment and Learning for All
register.detail: Approved 29 April 2021 · Investment project financing · Closing date 31 December 2025
register.text: Empowers young Angolans, especially girls, and improves the quality of learning for all students.

register.name: Sonangol receivables purchase facility
register.detail: Closed 28 January 2026 · Syndicated
register.note: For Sonangol’s operating and capital spending
register.text: A syndicated facility arranged by Afreximbank for Sonangol, the national oil company, to fund its projected operating and capital expenditure through export-linked trade structures that reduce its exposure to swings in the oil price.

register.name: Eastern Region Agricultural Value Chain Development Project
register.detail: Approved November 2025 · 2026 to 2031 · Six eastern provinces
register.note: $190.4 million AfDB loan, with Rome Process and Mattei Plan funds and a grant
register.text: Improved seed, irrigation, 3,000 farmer training schools, six agribusiness centres and 400 km of feeder roads in six eastern provinces, with 7,500 direct jobs and 1.2 million people expected to benefit. It goes to food, the standard that sets Angola’s Coverage.

register.name: Economic Governance and Resilience Support Programme, Phase I
register.detail: Approved November 2024 · Two-year reform programme
register.text: A loan for the first phase of a reform programme that strengthens fiscal governance and private-sector participation, with a focus on climate-resilient farming and on women, young people, persons with disabilities and low-income households.

register.name: Angola Youth Employment Project
register.detail: Approved July 2024 · 2025 to 2029
register.text: An African Development Bank loan to train more than 95,000 young people in digital technology and in skills for climate-smart agriculture and transport, and to support start-ups. It matters for livelihood.

register.name: Coastal Towns Inclusive Sanitation Project, Phase 1
register.detail: Approved June 2023 · Signed 3 October 2023
register.note: $75 million AfDB and $49.4 million Africa Growing Together Fund
register.text: Climate-resilient sanitation and the treatment of wastewater and faecal sludge for Benguela, Baía Farta, Catumbela and Lobito, home to 1.4 million people, with better household waste collection and sanitation in schools and health facilities.

register.name: UK Export Finance, four infrastructure projects
register.detail: Announced 8 September 2026 · Cabinda airport £371 million · Camama-Viana road £73 million · Uíge electrification £93 million · Huambo transmission line £118 million
register.note: Unlocks £167 million of UK supply contracts
register.text: UK Export Finance support for four projects, among them transmission lines and substations in Uíge province and a high-voltage line from Belém do Dango in Huambo to Lomaum in Benguela. The two power projects matter for energy.

register.name: Quilonga Grande Water System, Phase 2
register.detail: Announced 20 August 2026 · Export credit with Bpifrance Assurance Export cover · Sfil
register.note: A new treatment plant of 518,000 m³ a day
register.text: Financing for the Republic of Angola, arranged by Standard Chartered with cover from Bpifrance Assurance Export, for the second phase of the Quilonga Grande water system. The new plant is expected to bring reliable clean water to approximately five million people. It matters for water.

register.name: Lobito Atlantic Railway
register.detail: Announced 4 December 2024 · Signed 17 December 2025 · Financial close reported July 2026
register.note: Alongside up to $200 million from DBSA; rail line and mineral port
register.text: Finances the rehabilitation and operation of the mineral port in Lobito and about 1,300 km of rail from Lobito to Luau on the eastern border.

register.name: Project for Transmission System Reinforcement in Southern Region
register.detail: Signed 21 August 2025 · 1.20% for the project portion · 30 years with 10 years of grace
register.text: A JICA loan for new transmission lines and substations in southern Angola, including a 220 kV line between the Nombungo and Namibe substations, and for better distribution networks. It matters for energy.

register.name: Water treatment plants, southern Angola
register.detail: Announced 4 December 2024 · Political risk insurance
register.text: A DFC commitment of up to $150 million in political risk insurance for new water treatment plants serving underserved communities in southern Angola.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil
items.label: Oil rents, share of GDP, 2021
items.text: The revenue that has written the budget for a generation, and now backs far less of the debt.
items.alt: An offshore oil platform off Angola

items.name: The Corridor
items.label: Of rail from Lobito to Luau
items.text: Its rehabilitation is financed with $553 million from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation and up to $200 million from the Development Bank of Southern Africa, from the port of Lobito to Luau on the eastern border.

items.name: The Rivers
items.label: Of electricity from renewables, 2023
items.text: A clean grid, and 4,153 m³ of renewable fresh water per person.
items.alt: A hydroelectric dam on the Kwanza River

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: About 638,000 km² of forest and woodland.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Seven in ten live in cities.
items.alt: Families walking along the Marginal waterfront in Luanda at golden hour

items.name: Carrinho Group
items.text: An Angolan family-owned food group with 19 factories at the mouth of the Lobito corridor, making flour, pasta, edible oil, packaged foods and animal feed.

items.name: HabiTerra
items.text: The housing social enterprise of Development Workshop Angola. Working with Development Workshop Angola, KixiCredito and HabiTerra, Reall has supported the development of over 170 homes.

items.name: MCA solar minigrids
items.text: At Cazombo, 25.40 MWp of solar with 75.26 MWh of batteries, built to supply more than 136,000 people: the first park of the programme to be delivered.

items.name: 42 Luanda
items.text: A peer-to-peer coding campus, the first of its network in sub-Saharan Africa; nearly 25,000 applicants in its first three months.

items.name: Appy Saúde
items.text: Lets people order, pay for and receive medicines from the main pharmacies in Angola.

items.name: Jobartis
items.text: A job board founded in Luanda in 2013, now matching workers and employers in several African countries.

coverage.gap_text: Angolans below the Living Line for food: three in four are moderately or severely food insecure.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 75% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Water
guarantees.note: Basic water; safely managed water is not measured

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Outside urban slums; 63% of city dwellers live in slums; safe sanitation is not measured

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: About 530 kWh a person a year, against 1,000; 56% cook cleanly

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 42% complete lower secondary school; reading by age ten is not measured

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above US$4.20 a day; 54% live below it; dated
